title: Largest open where etale sections agree
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $F$ be a sheaf of sets on $S_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaf-of-sets]. Let $V\to S$ be an object of $S_{\Et}$ and $s,t\in F(V)$. For a morphism of schemes $a:T\to V$ with composite $e:T\to V\to S$, write $s|_T\in(e^{-1}F)(T)$ for the restriction of $e^*s\in(e^{-1}F)(V\times_ST)$ [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-composition-units] along the $T$-morphism $(a,\mathrm{id}_T):T\to V\times_ST$. Then there is a unique open subscheme $W\subset V$ such that a morphism $a:T\to V$ factors through $W$ if and only if $s|_T=t|_T$.

proof.text: On the etale site of $V$, define a subpresheaf $H$ of the final sheaf by putting $H(U)=\{\ast\}$ when the pullbacks of $s$ and $t$ to $U$ agree and $H(U)=\varnothing$ otherwise. Restrictions preserve agreement, and the sheaf equalizer axiom for $F$ shows that these local singleton sections glue; hence $H$ is a subsheaf of the final sheaf.

Apply the open-representability statement for subsheaves of the final etale sheaf to $H$. It gives a unique open subscheme $W\subset V$ such that an etale object $U\to V$ factors through $W$ exactly when the pullbacks of $s$ and $t$ to $U$ agree. Uniqueness of $W$ with the stated property for all morphisms $a:T\to V$ follows by testing on the open immersions $W\to V$ and $W'\to V$ of two candidates, which gives $W\subset W'\subset W$.

proof.text: For a geometric point $\bar{x}\to V$, the point lies in $W$ exactly when the germs of $s$ and $t$ in the stalk $F_{\bar{x}}$ agree: the stalk of $H$ is the singleton precisely in that case. For any morphism $a:T\to V$, the existing stalk-and-germ description of etale inverse images identifies the germ of the restricted section at a geometric point $\bar{y}\to T$ with the germ of $s$ (respectively $t$) at $a\bar{y}$. Thus $s|_T=t|_T$ implies every geometric point of $T$ maps into $W$, so $a$ factors through the open $W$; the converse follows from $s|_W=t|_W$ (Step 2): by the restriction compatibility (0) of the units, $(e^*s)|_{W\times_ST}=e^*(s|_W)=e^*(t|_W)=(e^*t)|_{W\times_ST}$, and $(a,\mathrm{id}_T)$ factors through $W\times_ST$. The stalks and germs used here are those of [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks].
